relations.myth: Sopdet guides Sah and the deceased along celestial paths
relations.note: Sopdet accompanies Sah and leads him and the deceased onto the sky’s perfect paths.
relations.source: Pyramid Texts, PT 442 and related recensions

relations.myth: Sah and Sopdet encircle the deceased
relations.note: Sopdet and Sah jointly encircle or escort the deceased.
Later astral theology presents Sah as Sopdet’s husband or consort.

relations.myth: Union of Sopdet and Osiris produces the morning star
relations.note: Sopdet unites with Osiris, manifested as the king or Sah, producing the morning star.
Plutarch pairs Sothis, Isis’s soul, with Orion, the soul of Osiris.
Sopdet becomes the explicit compound identity Isis-Sothis in later Egyptian theology.
The compound Isis-Sothis rides a dog representing Sirius in Roman-period iconography.
Later astral theology makes Sopdet and Sah the parents of Sopdu.
A divinized morning star is born from Sopdet’s union with the king or Osiris.
At the horizon Sopdet can be described as Re’s mother.
Sopdet rises before Re and nurses the sun at the horizon.
A Hibis inscription calls Sopdet the Eye of Re.
Through the Isis-Sothis equation, Sopdet becomes Horus’s mother in later theology.

relations.myth: Sopdet releases Hapy from his cavern
relations.note: Sopdet throws or pours Hapy from his cavern, bringing the inundation.
Some monuments fuse Sopdet with Satet through shared celestial, inundation, and iconographic functions.

relations.myth: Satet follows Sopdet’s cow in inundation procession
relations.note: Satet follows the Dendera Sopdet cow in an astronomical procession signifying inundation.
A Komir hymn addresses Anuket as Sothis who sends the inundation.

relations.myth: Anuket follows Sopdet’s cow in inundation procession
relations.note: Anuket follows the Dendera Sopdet cow in an astronomical procession signifying inundation.
Dendera identifies Hathor of Iunet as Sothis, sovereign of stars and queen of divine spirits.
BM EA 8539 identifies Nephthys as Sothis, lady of Ankhtawy.
An Edfu litany identifies Bastet, Tefnut, and Sothis as one divine form.
An Edfu litany identifies Tefnut, Bastet, and Sothis as one divine form.
A ritual hymn calls Weret-Hekau “Sothis of the flame.”

relations.myth: Sopdet traverses Nut’s body in the decanal cycle
relations.note: Sopdet disappears, travels, and is reborn within Nut’s celestial body.

relations.myth: Celestial opposition between southern and northern constellations
relations.note: Astronomical arrangements place Sopdet and Sah opposite or protected from the northern Foreleg constellation.
The divine king Darius offers wine to Sopdet and addresses her as his mother.
